# STM32H743 Nano FC + 4-in-1 80 A ESC (Job #88): Power-Stage Loss Model, Thermal Analysis, and Bidirectional DShot600 Timer/DMA Allocation

## 0. Scope and Assumptions

No MOSFET, gate driver, board size or burst profile was specified, so I've fixed a **reference design**. Every equation is parametric, so you can substitute datasheet values.

**Architecture.** The 48 kHz PWM is generated by the **ESC MCU** (AM32 or BLHeli_32 on an AT32F421 / STM32G071 class part), not by the H743. The H743 only produces DShot600 and receives eRPM telemetry. The two halves are modelled separately.

## 1. Conduction Loss Model

### 1.1 Topology

The ESC uses 6-step trapezoidal drive with complementary (synchronous) PWM. At every instant, exactly **two FETs carry the phase current**:
- the PWM'd high-side FET or its synchronous low-side complement, plus
- the fully-on low-side FET of the return phase.

Total conduction loss per motor channel:

$$P_{cond,ch} = 2\,I_{rms}^2\,R_{DS}(T_j), \qquad R_{DS}(T_j) = R_{25}\left[1+\alpha(T_j-25)\right]$$

where α ≈ 0.006 /K, giving k_T ≈ 1.45 at 100 °C.

**Ripple correction.** I_rms² = I² + ΔI²/12. The phase inductance is about 10 µH, so ΔI is roughly V·D(1−D)/(L·f) ≈ 4.7 A. The correction is under 0.03 % and is neglected.

### 1.2 Numbers at T_j = 100 °C

$$P_{cond,ch} = 2 \times 80^2 \times 1.45\times10^{-3} = \mathbf{18.6\ W\ per\ motor}$$

### 1.3 Per-FET distribution

Each FET is active for 1/3 of the electrical cycle. Electrical frequency is about 3.5 kHz for a 14-pole motor at 30 k rpm, far faster than FET thermal time constants, so averaging is valid.

| FET | Conduction expression | Loss |
|---|---|---|
| High side (PWM'd) | ⅓ · D · I²R | ⅓ · 0.9 · 9.28 W = **2.78 W** |
